title: Vanishing of Cech cohomology on a cofinal system of coverings implies vanishing of cohomology (any site)
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a site, $\mathcal B\subset\operatorname{Ob}(\mathcal C)$ a set of objects, $\mathrm{Cov}$ a set of coverings of $\mathcal C$, and $\mathcal F\in\textit{Ab}(\mathcal C)$; $H^p(U,-)$ is cohomology over an object [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] and $\check H^p$ Cech cohomology [def-weil-pbc-site-cech-complex]. Assume: (1) for every $\mathcal U=\{U_t\to U\}_{t\in T}$ in $\mathrm{Cov}$ the objects $U$, $U_t$ and all $U_{t_0}\times_U\cdots\times_UU_{t_p}$ ($p\ge0$, $t_k\in T$; the fibre products chosen in [def-weil-pbc-site-cech-complex]) lie in $\mathcal B$; (2) for every $U\in\mathcal B$ the coverings of $U$ occurring in $\mathrm{Cov}$ are cofinal among all coverings of $U$ (every covering $\{V_j\to U\}_{j\in J}$ of $U$ is refined by some $\{U_t\to U\}_{t\in T}\in\mathrm{Cov}$: for every $t$ there are $j$ and a morphism $U_t\to V_j$ over $U$); (3) $\check H^p(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)=0$ for all $\mathcal U\in\mathrm{Cov}$ and $p>0$. Then $H^p(U,\mathcal F)=0$ for all $p>0$ and all $U\in\mathcal B$. (General-site version of [lem-weil-pbc-cech-vanishing-criterion], which is stated for the small etale site; same proof: embed $\mathcal F$ into an injective, Lemma 03AW, Lemma 03F8, dimension shifting.)

source.place: Lemma Tag 03F9 (lemma-cech-vanish-collection) and its proof (Lemma Tag 03AW lemma-injective-trivial-cech, Lemma Tag 03F8 lemma-ses-cech-h1)

proof.text: **Step 1 (the induction).** Fix $\mathcal B$ and $\mathrm{Cov}$ satisfying (1) and (2). Call an abelian sheaf $\mathcal G\in\textit{Ab}(\mathcal C)$ *Cech-acyclic on* $\mathrm{Cov}$ if $\check H^p(\mathcal U,\mathcal G)=0$ for all $p>0$ and all $\mathcal U\in\mathrm{Cov}$, i.e. if $\mathcal G$ satisfies (3). For $p\ge1$ let $P(p)$ be the assertion: for every abelian sheaf $\mathcal G$ Cech-acyclic on $\mathrm{Cov}$ and every $U\in\mathcal B$, $H^p(U,\mathcal G)=0$. We prove $P(p)$ for all $p\ge1$ by induction on $p$, the assertion being quantified over all such $\mathcal G$ at once (Steps 2-6 for a fixed $\mathcal G$, Step 7 the induction); the lemma is $P(p)$ for $\mathcal G=\mathcal F$, which is Cech-acyclic on $\mathrm{Cov}$ by (3).

source.place: Lemma Tag 03F9, proof ("We will indicate this by saying F has vanishing higher Cech cohomology for any U in Cov"; "Since F was an arbitrary abelian sheaf with vanishing higher Cech cohomology ... And so on and so forth")

proof.text: **Step 2 (embedding into an injective).** Let $\mathcal G$ be Cech-acyclic on $\mathrm{Cov}$. Since $\textit{Ab}(\mathcal C)$ is an abelian category with enough injectives [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaves-enough-injectives], choose a monomorphism $\mathcal G\to\mathcal I$ with $\mathcal I$ an injective object of $\textit{Ab}(\mathcal C)$ [def-sp-injective-resolutions], and let $\mathcal Q=\mathcal I/\mathcal G$ be its cokernel in $\textit{Ab}(\mathcal C)$ [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], so that $0\to\mathcal G\to\mathcal I\to\mathcal Q\to0$ is a short exact sequence of abelian sheaves.

source.place: Lemma Tag 03F9, proof, first paragraph ("Choose an embedding F -> I into an injective abelian sheaf ... Let Q = I/F so that we have a short exact sequence")

proof.text: **Step 3 ($\mathcal I$ is Cech-acyclic).** By [lem-weil-pbc-site-injective-cech-acyclic] (Stacks 03AW), $\check H^p(\mathcal U,\mathcal I)=0$ for every $p>0$ and every covering $\mathcal U$ of $\mathcal C$, in particular for every $\mathcal U\in\mathrm{Cov}$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 03F9, proof ("By Lemma 03AW I has vanishing higher Cech cohomology for any U in Cov")

proof.text: **Step 4 (sections over objects of $\mathcal B$).** Let $U\in\mathcal B$. The sequence $0\to\mathcal G(U)\to\mathcal I(U)\to\mathcal Q(U)\to0$ is exact. Exactness at $\mathcal G(U)$ and $\mathcal I(U)$: $H^n(U,-)=R^n\Gamma(U,-)$ are the right derived functors of the left exact additive functor $v=\Gamma(U,-):\textit{Ab}(\mathcal C)\to\textit{Ab}$, $\mathcal G\mapsto\mathcal G(U)$ [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]; the long exact sequence of right derived functors [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-long-exact] of the sequence of Step 2 begins with the exact $0\to R^0v(\mathcal G)\to R^0v(\mathcal I)\to R^0v(\mathcal Q)$, and $R^0v\cong v$ naturally [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-universal-delta-functor], so $0\to\mathcal G(U)\to\mathcal I(U)\to\mathcal Q(U)$ is exact. Surjectivity of $\mathcal I(U)\to\mathcal Q(U)$: let $\Sigma$ be the set of coverings of $U$ belonging to $\mathrm{Cov}$; by (2) it is a cofinal system of coverings of $U$, and $\check H^1(\mathcal U,\mathcal G)=0$ for every $\mathcal U\in\Sigma$ because $\mathcal G$ is Cech-acyclic on $\mathrm{Cov}$; so [lem-weil-pbc-site-ses-cech-h1-surjective] (Stacks 03F8), applied to $0\to\mathcal G\to\mathcal I\to\mathcal Q\to0$ and $\Sigma$, gives that $\mathcal I(U)\to\mathcal Q(U)$ is surjective.

source.place: Lemma Tag 03F9, proof ("By Lemma 03F8 and our assumption (2) this sequence gives rise to an exact sequence 0 -> F(U) -> I(U) -> Q(U) -> 0 for every U in B")

proof.text: **Step 5 (short exact sequence of Cech complexes).** Let $\mathcal U=\{U_t\to U\}_{t\in T}\in\mathrm{Cov}$. The morphisms $\mathcal G\to\mathcal I\to\mathcal Q$ induce morphisms of Cech complexes $\check{\mathcal C}^\bullet(\mathcal U,\mathcal G)\to\check{\mathcal C}^\bullet(\mathcal U,\mathcal I)\to\check{\mathcal C}^\bullet(\mathcal U,\mathcal Q)$ (functoriality, part (e) of [def-weil-pbc-site-cech-complex]); the exactness statement of (e) cannot be used, since $0\to\mathcal G\to\mathcal I\to\mathcal Q\to0$ need not be exact in $\textit{PAb}(\mathcal C)$. In degree $p\ge0$ the sequence is the product over $\mathbf t=(t_0,\ldots,t_p)\in T^{p+1}$ of the sequences $0\to\mathcal G(U_{\mathbf t})\to\mathcal I(U_{\mathbf t})\to\mathcal Q(U_{\mathbf t})\to0$ with $U_{\mathbf t}=U_{t_0}\times_U\cdots\times_UU_{t_p}$; by (1) every $U_{\mathbf t}$ lies in $\mathcal B$, so each factor is short exact by Step 4, and a product of short exact sequences of abelian groups is short exact (kernel and image of a product of homomorphisms are the products of the kernels and images); in degrees $p<0$ all terms are $0$. Hence $0\to\check{\mathcal C}^\bullet(\mathcal U,\mathcal G)\to\check{\mathcal C}^\bullet(\mathcal U,\mathcal I)\to\check{\mathcal C}^\bullet(\mathcal U,\mathcal Q)\to0$ is a short exact sequence of cochain complexes of abelian groups, short exactness of complexes being degreewise [lem-weil-pbc-cochain-complexes-degreewise-exact].

source.place: Lemma Tag 03F9, proof ("Hence for any U in Cov we get a short exact sequence of Cech complexes ... since each term in the Cech complex is made up out of a product of values over elements of B by assumption (1)")

proof.text: **Step 6 ($\mathcal Q$ is Cech-acyclic).** For $\mathcal U\in\mathrm{Cov}$, the long exact cohomology sequence [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-homology-long-exact] of the short exact sequence of Step 5 contains, for each $p\ge1$, the exact piece $\check H^p(\mathcal U,\mathcal I)\to\check H^p(\mathcal U,\mathcal Q)\xrightarrow{\delta^p}\check H^{p+1}(\mathcal U,\mathcal G)$. The left term is $0$ by Step 3 and the right term is $0$ since $\mathcal G$ is Cech-acyclic on $\mathrm{Cov}$ and $p+1>0$; so $\check H^p(\mathcal U,\mathcal Q)=0$. Thus $\mathcal Q$ is again an abelian sheaf Cech-acyclic on $\mathrm{Cov}$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 03F9, proof ("In particular we have a long exact sequence of Cech cohomology groups ... This implies that Q is also an abelian sheaf with vanishing higher Cech cohomology for all U in Cov")

proof.text: **Step 7 (dimension shifting).** Let $U\in\mathcal B$ and apply the long exact sequence of the derived functors $H^n(U,-)=R^n\Gamma(U,-)$ [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-long-exact] to $0\to\mathcal G\to\mathcal I\to\mathcal Q\to0$; since $\mathcal I$ is injective, $H^n(U,\mathcal I)=0$ for $n>0$ [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-injective-vanishing]. Case $p=1$: the piece $H^0(U,\mathcal I)\to H^0(U,\mathcal Q)\to H^1(U,\mathcal G)\to H^1(U,\mathcal I)=0$ is exact, and under the natural isomorphism $H^0(U,-)\cong\Gamma(U,-)$ [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-universal-delta-functor] its first map is $\mathcal I(U)\to\mathcal Q(U)$, surjective by Step 4; hence $H^1(U,\mathcal G)=0$. This holds for every $\mathcal G$ Cech-acyclic on $\mathrm{Cov}$ and every $U\in\mathcal B$, which is $P(1)$. Case $p\ge2$, assuming $P(p-1)$: the piece $H^{p-1}(U,\mathcal Q)\to H^p(U,\mathcal G)\to H^p(U,\mathcal I)=0$ is exact, and $H^{p-1}(U,\mathcal Q)=0$ by $P(p-1)$ applied to $\mathcal Q$, which is Cech-acyclic on $\mathrm{Cov}$ by Step 6; hence $H^p(U,\mathcal G)=0$, which is $P(p)$. By induction $P(p)$ holds for all $p\ge1$; with $\mathcal G=\mathcal F$ (Step 1) this is the lemma.

source.place: Lemma Tag 03F9, proof, last paragraph (long exact cohomology sequence; H^n(U,I)=0 for n>0 by Derived Categories Lemma 015B; H^1(U,F)=0; H^1(U,Q)=0; H^2(U,F)=0, and so on)

split_report.summary: Statement checked against Stacks sites-cohomology Lemma 03F9 (lemma-cech-vanish-collection): kept, with two clarifications that do not change its meaning: the fibre products in (1) are the ones chosen in def-weil-pbc-site-cech-complex (B is a set of objects, not closed under isomorphism), and 'cofinal' in (2) spelled out as refinement over U. Proof written from Stacks' proof of 03F9 (read in full; it uses dimension shifting, not the Cech-to-cohomology spectral sequence 03AZ or the map 03AX), in the same seven steps as the reviewed small-etale-site version lem-weil-pbc-cech-vanishing-criterion, with general-site nodes: enough injectives lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaves-enough-injectives, 03AW lem-weil-pbc-site-injective-cech-acyclic (existing, claimed by group C, cited only), 03F8 as the new node lem-weil-pbc-site-ses-cech-h1-surjective, R^0 = Gamma by lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-universal-delta-functor (instead of lem-sp-derived-well-defined, stated for Grothendieck abelian categories), the general long exact sequence of derived functors, vanishing on injectives and the Cech long exact sequence (Mathlib leaves). Step 5 notes why the exactness clause of the Cech-complex definition cannot be used (the sheaf sequence is not exact as presheaves): exactness comes from Step 4 on objects of B and hypothesis (1). Step 1 is elementary (set-up of the induction); the rest cite nodes. Mathlib (three kinds plus loogle) has Sheaf.H, H' and cechComplexFunctor but no criterion.
